threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare at the bus timings like they matter, instead of just accepting you'll wait 20 mins in the rain.
Last Saturday, the 196 bus was packed with folks singing old reggae tunes. Even the driver was smiling, but I swear I saw a pigeon trying to join in.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of shisha and fresh kebabs became the background of my evening walks, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find street art galleries behind every corner here, but only in Friedrichshain can you watch a mural transform overnight with just a spray can and some creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid 24th Street during rush hour once BART’s down. Those just working here are still stuck in traffic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a bus driver kiss their partner goodbye as passengers boarded, then drive off while still wiping a tear. Only in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all of Gràcia is just for selfies, but real life happens in the small plazas after dark, full of laughter and secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the flock of fresh-faced folks fumbling with the metro map while blocking the escalators near Joanic station. Classic sign!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You call it a 'corner shop' instead of a 'newsagent' and don't know the unwritten rule about queuing at the post office. Classic rookie move.
Heard a couple arguing about who left the last bottle of wine at the bus stop. Turns out it was a bottle of vinegar. Classic Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy set up a mobile disco in the park, blasting techno while kids flew kites. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you get a döner and simultaneously hear a live band jamming in the street. It's like a perfect soundtrack to late-night snacking.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's from here by how they get annoyed at tourists taking selfies in front of the Mission murals during rush hour.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 19 Polk singing opera to a packed bus. Everyone went from annoyed to entertained in seconds. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but it’s the cendros on Carrer de Verdi that hum with real local life, especially at dusk.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by their map fixation—standing on the corner of Carrer de València, searching for directions like it’s a treasure map.
